\n\nI'm now focusing on the target audience and overall vibe. It's becoming clear this should be mobile-first with a Bill Wurtz aesthetic - think neon, simple graphics, and rapid-fire humor. I'm nailing down the key features, specifically a swipeable slide mechanism to showcase funny image summaries generated from the video. Gemini API will be critical for generating the text and images that encapsulate the video's quirky essence. I'm solidifying the tech stack to React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide React.


**Developing the Gemini Prompt**

\n\nI'm now diving into the AI integration. I plan to leverage Gemini Pro (`gemini-2.5-flash`) to generate humorous slide content, assuming the user provides a YouTube link. **Refining Game Mechanics**

\n\nI'm now pivoting from generating the *game content* to generating the *game code*. The user's goal isn't to *play* a generated game, but to get a React app that *uses* Gemini to generate content, namely text and image prompts for slide content. Real-time image generation seems slow and expensive for a demo, so I'm considering placeholder images with Gemini-generated text overlays for now. This will allow for rapid iteration and user feedback.


**Prioritizing Image Generation**

\n\nI'm now focusing on leveraging Gemini's image generation capabilities directly. This is the most compelling avenue to achieve the desired visual style. \n\nI'm now solidifying the implementation steps. The initial setup includes basic theming and the core swipe functionality with Framer Motion. I'll then integrate Gemini for text generation, starting with "History of Japan" content, and then add image generation as a subsequent step. I'll add a "generate game" button on the home screen which builds slides using content from the specific YouTube video. The UI will have a vaporwave/Bill Wurtz aesthetic, neon colors, and bold text. The `gemini.ts` file will house the `generateStory` and `generateImage` functions, crucial for pulling content. I'm also now shifting from thinking about a default content store to making sure the content is generated by Gemini every single time, as the user wants to test the capability of generating new ones on the spot. I need to iron out the image batch loading flow.


**Defining Final Implementation Plan**

\n\nI'm now nailing down the specifics for the final product. The "Loading" phase is becoming part of the experience, not a nuisance.  I have defined the `gemini.ts` with  `generateStoryboard` and `generateSlideImage` functions. The `Deck.tsx` handles the swiping, and `App.tsx` orchestrates everything. I'm aiming for a dark mode with neon text visual style. The default content will be "The History of Japan (Bill Wurtz style)". I'm focusing on text generation and then image generation in the background. I plan to display a loading progress bar to give the user immediate feedback. I'm focusing on ensuring seamless integration of the `framer-motion` library for smooth swipe animations. Regardless of direct access, I'm confident Gemini can summarize it effectively. I will provide the URL/ID and rely on the model for content generation or humorous fabrication.
